commit.message:
Check signals in loops that dispatch no commands

When a loop body is empty or executes the incr fast-path optimization,
Jim_EvalObj returns immediately without evaluating any actual command,
which means the per-command signal check is never reached. This allows
an async signal handler to be ignored indefinitely in such loops.

Add signal checks in Jim_EvalObj after both optimization paths return,
ensuring that async signals can interrupt loops regardless of whether
the body dispatches any actual command.

Fixes #385
